chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: location fits event-to-place relation for all instances.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: entertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An entertainment business relation between a perform action and the entertainment business where the action occurred. Also called "venue", "performance location", "showplace". Examples: "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Concert Hall'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Theater Royal'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Comedy Club'". Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any place an action occurs.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: typicalAgeRange
candidates.comment: A typical age range relation between a creative work or event and the expected age group of its audience. Also called age suitability, target age, recommended age. Examples: "Book typicalAgeRange '7-9'", "Movie typicalAgeRange '13+'", "Event typicalAgeRange 'all ages'".

candidates.label: requiredMinAge
candidates.comment: A required minimum age relation between a people audience and the lower age limit for inclusion. Also called min age, age requirement. Examples: "An adult event targets a people audience with required min age '18'.", "A driving course has a required min age '16'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required min age '65'."

candidates.label: populationType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute indicating the common type of individuals or cases within a statistical population or variable. Also called demographic group, target group, study population. Examples: A statistical population has a population type of 'Adults'. A statistical variable has a population type of 'Children aged 5-12'. The study focuses on a population type of 'Patients with Condition X'.

candidates.label: requiredMaxAge
candidates.comment: A required maximum age relation between a people audience and the upper age limit for inclusion. Also called max age, age limit. Examples: "A children's event targets a people audience with required max age '12'.", "A youth program has a required max age '25'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required max age '99'."

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: suggestedMinAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the minimum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "minimum age", "lower age limit", "age floor". Examples: "The game has suggestedMinAge 7", "The audience specification includes suggestedMinAge 18", "This content is suitable from suggestedMinAge 3.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMaxAge, which specifies only the maximum.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: yearsInOperation
candidates.comment: An operational age relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, indicating the number of years the business has been active. Also called business age, operational duration, years active. Examples: TargetAudience yearsInOperation "5-10 years", BusinessAudience yearsInOperation "over 20 years", StartupAudience yearsInOperation "under 2 years".

candidates.label: suggestedMaxAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: childMinAge
candidates.comment: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the minimal age of a child. Also called "minimum child age", "lower age limit for child", "child age floor". Examples: "Parent audience for infants childMinAge 0", "Parent audience for school-age children childMinAge 5". Distinct from childMaxAge, which specifies the maximal age.
